newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Eurodollars end higher on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Eurodollars end higher on short-covering.

text.p: SIMEX Eurodollar futures ended higher on the back of gains in U.S. Treasury bonds in Tokyo trade on Monday as players realised they had over-reacted to comments by the Federal Reserve chairman last week.
"What (Alan) Greenspan said was just a little bit of a scare but no more than that," said a trader with a U.S. futures house.

Greenspan's remark that the Fed had to be wary of "irrational exuberance" infecting U.S. stock and other asset markets re-ignited fears of an interest rate hike and caused world financial markets to tumble on Friday.

He also said that while inflation has been low, its future course remained uncertain. But weaker-than-expected U.S. November employment data provided some support to the bond market as players took heart in the idea that the economy was not gathering steam.
"Technically, there's still room to the upside," said the trader, adding that March Eurodollars showed potential to reach 94.52 and June, 94.44.
The March contract finished at 94.50 against its IMM close at 94.47. June was at 94.40 against 94.36. Turnover for both months was over 12,000 lots.
"This is the calm after the storm but it doesn't mean there isn't another storm coming," said a trader with an Asian house.
Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures also edged up on the back of the recovery in U.S. bonds, but volumes were low amid a dearth of fresh domestic leads.
"A little confidence was regained watching U.S. treasuries going up," said the trader at the U.S. institution.
June Euroyen stood at 99.34 at 1115 GMT against its IMM close at 99.33. It is expected to trade within a range of 99.28-99.35.
March JGBs settled at 125.82 against their opening 125.70.
